body: I kindly asked @dsnopek to test and they confirmed the issue. Thank you, David!

I tried building with an earlier version of Emscripten (3.1.74) but that didn't fix the problem. When the editor is stuck, I tried pausing and playing the debugger a couple times (to make sure it was stuck in the same spot), and it seems like it might be stuck waiting on a mutex in `EditorExportPlatformAndroid::~EditorExportPlatformAndroid()`: I don't have debug symbols loaded, so it's a little hard to see, but I think that's this line: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/c6d130abd9188f313e6701d01a0ddd6ea32166a0/platform/android/export/export_plugin.cpp#L4256 It's also a little weird that this is in the destructor? I'm not sure why that would be happening when loading the project, so maybe it's actually the project manager unloading? This may be a red herring, but I figured I'd share it just in case

Also happens for me with commit c6d130a on macOS Sequoia 15.5 with an M4 Pro chip on Chrome 138.0.7204.94. This is the output I see in the JavaScript Console – I don't think there's anything particularly useful in there, but I'm including it just in case. I may be able to test some earlier commits to see if I can pin down where the issue is introduced.

My testing results (will update):

- 09ea7bc6a3 (17 Apr 2025) - Not reproducible
- be3ecaeb3c (19 May 2025) - Not reproducible
- 99f5a3d665 (27 May 2025) - Not reproducible
- de37627404 (28 May 2025) - Not reproducible
- eb72ce2db4 (30 May 2025) - Not reproducible
- **2df41d8144 (31 May 2025) - Reproducible**
- 167a9e33d3 (2 Jun 2025) - Reproducible
- e45cc68092 (2 Jun 2025, try 2) - Reproducible

Looks like the bug may have been introduced by 2df41d8144, but it would be good to have some others confirm it

I'll share some of my findings so far. The issue is "resolved" when reverting #104458, but I don't want to do so without totally first understanding the issue in depth. So far, I managed to run #104458 with the following changes: 1. Forcing [`godot_js_os_thread_pool_size_get()`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/c6d130abd9188f313e6701d01a0ddd6ea32166a0/platform/web/js/libs/library_godot_os.js#L351-L360) to return `1`. 2. Adding the build param `proxy_to_pthread=yes`. (1) would defeat the purpose of #104458, and (2) prevents the use of GDExtensions so far. It seems that with the change of the thread pool size has some unknown side effects. It seems that the main thread is waiting for a thread, but the thread checks for another object's value. Their `EditorExportPlatformAndroid` pointer don't seem to point to the same address. That would explain why setting the `SafeFlag` in the main thread doesn't seem to affect the waited thread. | Main thread | Thread method | | :---: | :---: | | | | I even tested casting the memory of both addresses, and it fits. There's two assigned`EditorExportPlatformAndroid`.

I found out pretty much the issue: we're experiencing a deadlock because not enough threads are available. The latest thread "started" is considered started without really being it, so the main threads waits for it eternally.

I'm pasting here [what I said in the Godot Developers Chat](https://chat.godotengine.org/channel/web?msg=taJ6zkpZkKoyJpgCR):

>So, the current issue is this. 
>
>1. [#104458](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/104458) introduced a change that made `OS_Web::get_default_thread_pool_size()` return something else than `1` (in this case `4`).
>2. This enables `WorkerThreadPool` to create `4` threads, `3` max low-priority.
>3. Four threads are created for the pool.
>4. `EditorExportPlatformAndroid` is instantiated a first time, I think it's for metadata purposes. [A thread (`check_for_changes_thread`) is started in the constructor](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/c6d130abd9188f313e6701d01a0ddd6ea32166a0/platform/android/export/export_plugin.cpp#L4247) (id `16`).
>5. Other threads are started elsewhere.
>6. `EditorExportPlatformAndroid` is instantiated a second time. `check_for_changes_thread` is started in the constructor (id `20`). The thing is that it doesn't start because there's an hard limit of `8` emscripten threads (set in the build).
>7. The second `EditorExportPlatformAndroid` destructor is called. As `check_for_changes_thread.is_started()` returns `true` (because it has a thread ID even if it hasn't really started yet), [`check_for_changes_thread.wait_to_finish()` gets called](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/c6d130abd9188f313e6701d01a0ddd6ea32166a0/platform/android/export/export_plugin.cpp#L4256).
>8. The editor deadlocks. (the only thread running relating to `EditorExportPlatformAndroid` is thread `16`, but `20` is waiting indefinitely for its thread to end, but it didn't even started.)

And I followed [with this](https://chat.godotengine.org/channel/web?msg=9LLyfEdzguXEi7kZb):

>I think I know what happens. We don't limit the number of threads, but here's what emscripten says about `-sPTHREAD_POOL_SIZE`.
>
>>Optionally, pass the linker flag `-sPTHREAD_POOL_SIZE=<expression>` to specify a predefined pool of web workers to populate at page `preRun` time before application `main()` is called. This is important because if the workers do not already exist then we may need to wait for the next browser event iteration for certain things, see below.
>
>Here's what happens: in the same cycle, the editor is created and destructed. So the thread is waiting to be created next frame by the main thread, but the destructor is blocking the latter waiting for the non-started thread to finish.

> EditorExportPlatformAndroid is instantiated a first time, I think it's for metadata purposes.

First one seems to be real instance used by editor, and second time it is instantiated by `DocTools::generate()`. While it is not the core of the issue by itself, we probably should not start unnecessary threads when generating docs.
